candidates.text:
If you sat me on a lie detector, and asked me:

“Do you consider Coca-Cola a health drink?”

I will answer without hesitation and without blinking:

YES!

- anxiolytic
- kills headaches/migraines
- performance enhancer 
- settles nausea
- raises T
- helps dissolve shit in your stomach
- 

etc.

Now, before some 0 IQ nutrition autist starts hyperventilating:

Am I presenting a balanced scientific assessment of Coca-Cola?

Obviously not. (Even though, all of those are documented effects). But rather, my larger point is:

I CHOOSE THE FRAME.

Because your belief about something can often exert an influence over your experience of that thing SO POWERFUL that it appears to OVERRIDE the underlying material “facts.”

There are experiments on this that may change the way you think about mind and body.

I’ll tell you about one in the 1960s:

Japanese schoolboys hypersensitive to leaves from lacquer/wax trees, plants which produce a dermatitis similar to poison ivy.

Researchers touch one arm with a HARMLESS leaf and they tell the boys:

“This is the poisonous one.”

RASH.
Redness. Itching. Inflammation.
Then they do the opposite.

Actually touch them with the poisonous leaf…
And tell them:

“Don’t worry. This one is harmless.”

Most of them DIDN’T REACT.
Read that again.

The nervous system was given one material reality…

And one BELIEVED reality…

In many cases, the body behaved according to the latter.

What the fuck do you do with that?

People like to IMAGINE that they experience reality directly. But they don’t. Nobody does.

Your nervous system is constantly interpreting.

Predicting.

Assigning meaning.

“This is dangerous.”

“This is good for me.”

“This person hates me.”

“I am getting sick.”

“This medication will save me.”

“I always perform badly under pressure.”

“I’m terrible with women.”

“I have bad genetics.”

And then your body and behaviour begin organising themselves AROUND THE EXPECTATION.

This is why I am so passionate and insistent, having drilled this into your heads for years now.

Your beliefs are everything.

A belief is not some cute sentence floating around inside your head.

Beliefs alter attention.
Attention alters perception.
Perception alters physiology and behaviour.
Behaviour alters outcomes.

Outcomes then come back around and reinforce the ORIGINAL BELIEF.

And eventually you look at the accumulated evidence and say:

“See? I knew it.”

Of course you fucking knew it.

You’ve been manufacturing evidence for it for ten years. What did you expect?

This does NOT mean you can believe cyanide is protein powder and live.

Material reality exists.

But understand…

You NEVER interact with material reality without an INTERPRETATION of material reality riding on top of it.

And that interpretation has the power to entirely DICTATE how we respond to it.

Placebo.

Nocebo.

Expectation.

Suggestion.

Hypnosis.

Self-image.

Different doors that invite the same question:

HOW MUCH OF WHAT YOU EXPERIENCE AS “REALITY” IS ACTUALLY YOUR NERVOUS SYSTEM OBEYING AN INSTRUCTION?

So yes.

I drink lots of Coke, and it ONLY adds to my health.

And I’m sure the alleged “healthmaxxers” who are obsessed with balls and deathly afraid of touching receipts would disagree.

Then again, a Big Mac would probably kill them. Thats fine.
They can keep their neurotic little story about it.

I like mine better….

Be VERY fucking careful what you decide things mean.

PERCEPTION IS REALITY.

Dario calling it “pacing” rather than “pause” or “slowdown” was brilliant

The existing framings have so much baggage that people can’t move past the old arguments and tribal blocs

If he had said “pause” he would’ve had to fight through the definition before anyone would engage with the argument, or been immediately written off as a decel

Coining “pacing” as a new frame creates a new category and performs a kind of (partial) frame reset. People don’t have a clear template to fit it to, so they’re forced to engage with the arguments on their own terms

The clean rhetorical slate resets old factions, and I think it’s partly why we’re seeing Dario, Sam, Elon all agreeing for the first time in a while

Went to a book fair in Abu Dhabi today and found the Roald Dahl book to which this Twitter-viral page belongs. It’s a short book for a grown-up, so I managed to relax after a long day and finish the book in 30 odd minutes.

The only Roald Dahl books I’d read before was the Chocolate Factory series, so this one was a pleasant surprise. With every single page I read, all I could see were things that wouldn’t be so freely authored today:

1/ The book title in itself

2/ The descriptions of these characters

3/ 75% of the word choice in the book would be considered “inappropriate” for kids

4/ The ending, which showed evil people getting well-deserved consequences (because all today’s media cares about is a chance at redemption).

I also learnt through the intro that Roald Dahl was not only an author, but also a chocolate historian, spy and airforce fighter, and later in life also helped develop a medical device to help kids! 

Most people can barely sustain one of such intense careers… No wonder he was so witty, one of the best storytellers of all time! 

P.S. He was also an inventor of words, and invented 500+ of those across his works. What a life he lived!

candidates.text:
So, the Navier Stokes equation was solved by AI. 

BUT, it was solved by brute force. 

It was not solved by an original insight. 

Einstein’s reframing of gravity from a pulling force to a geometric (curvature) effect of space and time was truly original
and mindblowing. 

It was one single insight. 

The prediction of time dilation and twin paradoxes was also borne of one single insight. 

As compute gets cheaper we will solve more brute force problems. 

(Isn’t ‘brute force’ another word for experimentation?)

Physics has the experimental science aspect - where AI will excel. 

Then there are the theoretical physicists. 

Still, we are not anywhere close to the kind of theoretical physics insight that Einstein or Newton generated. 

If AI can reconcile quantum theory and general relativity, then AGI is here. 

That is another test for AGI. 

That test won’t pass in the next 5 years is my view, and probably a lot longer.

“The old claim that money stops mattering after $75K / year was wrong. A 2023 study settled a decade-long argument between two researchers and found that happiness keeps rising with income, with no ceiling in sight. The exception was a small group, about 20 percent, who were already unhappy.

The mechanism is not about luxury. People with more money have fewer daily stressors. They do not worry about rent. A car repair does not require a credit card.
